hypothesis.cheapest_refuting_observation: The second site at +0xc8 is the SAME shape with a different stride, so probe it first with the association form alone and read `fndiff --ops`: if the `replace T[50:51]@c8-cc=['lwz'] O[48:50]@c0-c8=['addi','lwzx']` cluster does not move, the split is decided downstream of the source expression and both sites are allocator-side.
hypothesis.screened_against_target: yes — both sites were read in the aligned view and the target's form is `add rD,rBASE,rIV` followed by `lwz rD2,<const>(rD)` at each. Not screened: whether any parenthesisation of the address expression survives MWCC's reassociation at all.
hypothesis.statement: The two `lwzx` clusters are the same mechanism at two sites (+0x64 and +0xc8) and both have the shape `base + <IV> + <constant displacement>` where OUR build folds the constant into the index register (`addi r0,r3,1176` then `lwzx r0,r31,r0`) and the target folds it into the LOAD (`add r4,r31,r3` then `lwz r0,1176(r4)`). The untried construct class is therefore not the cursor local (measured dead) but the ASSOCIATION of the address expression: our source writes `*(s32*)(state + slot * 36 + 1176)`, one flat sum, so MWCC is free to reassociate; writing it as `*(s32*)((u8*)(state + slot * 36) + 1176)` or as a member load through a typed view forces the base+displacement split without adding a declaration.
